meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction; Registered Domicile in Panama City)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law codified system with Common Law-inspired Private Interest Foundation and trust doctrine under Ley 25 de 1995, plus autonomous public law components
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, effective 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Ley 32 de 2011); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama AML/CFT regime); Decreto de Gabinete No. 1 de 8 de febrero de 2016 (Unidad de Analisis Financiero - UAF); Ley 47 de 23 de diciembre de 2020 (beneficial ownership reporting duties); Ley 55 de 17 de abril de 2023 (Beneficial Owner Registry and Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros - SUSEF); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 129 de 17 de junio de 2020 (AML/CFT implementing regulation); applicable SUSEF and UAF risk-based guidelines and circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or civil registry authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a party, effective since 2008) or, for non-apostille states, consular legalization at the Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incorporation of a corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the founding state or Registro Publico de Panama for domestic corporate founders

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of Beneficial Owners extract of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent beneficial owner registry of the founding state (SUSEF for Panama domestic entities)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or board minutes authorizing the incorporation of the foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate founder's registered agent or notarial authority in the founding state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source of funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking institution holding the founder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer certification plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (Antecedentes Penales) for Foundation Council members and Protector
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of all non-Spanish foundation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Authorized Public Translator (Traductor Publico Autorizado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized translation certification appended to the apostilled or consularized source document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of the Founder, Protector, Foundation Council and any beneficial owner against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU and UK consolidated lists, and Panama's Lista de Personas y Entidades Relacionadas maintained by the UAF; PEPs identified by function or association trigger enhanced due diligence, compliance officer approval at the resident agent, and additional source-of-wealth documentation under Ley 23 de 2015, Decreto Ejecutivo 129 de 2020 and SUSEF/UAF guidelines; audit trail retention for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Online Name Reservation and Non-Conflict Certificate module (Ventanilla Electronica, https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory principle: each foundation must bear a distinctive denomination that cannot be identical or so similar to existing corporate or foundation names as to mislead; denominations are entered in Latin alphabetic script; non-Latin-script founders must submit a Spanish-Romanized transliteration; the deed must append the mandatory disclaimer Fundacion de Interes Privado (FIP) or the English-equivalent Private Interest Foundation formed under Ley 25 de 1995.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying banking, credit, finance, securities or insurance activity (Banco, Bank, Financiera, Seguros, Insurance, Trust Company, Fideicomiso, Bolsa, Valores) absent a licence from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama or Superintendencia de Seguros
Words reserved to the Panamanian State or international organizations (Republica de Panama, Gobierno, Nacional, Estado, Naciones Unidas, Fondo Monetario Internacional)
Denominations confusingly identical or similar to a pre-existing trademark or trade name protected at the Ministry of Commerce and Industries industrial property registry
Expressions contrary to public order, morality or good customs
Misleading terms representing public charity, official accreditation or government export-promotion functions for a private interest foundation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Formal SOP: (1) obtain the written rejection notice with the Registro Publico certificate reference; (2) file a Recurso de Reconsideracion within five business days before the Director of the Registration Department; (3) if denied, file a Recurso de Apelacion within ten business days before the Director General del Registro Publico, attaching trademark prior-search evidence from the Direccion de Registro de la Propiedad Industrial of the Ministry of Commerce and Industries; (4) if the administrative appeal is denied, submit an annulment action before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia; concurrently, immediately re-reserve an alternate transliteration to avoid expiry of the 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. A Private Interest Foundation may maintain its statutory domicile at the address of its licensed resident agent; no local physical branch, premises or employees are mandatory for an ISIC 6201 cloud-based helpdesk SaaS activity conducted from abroad. The resident agent must keep the foundation records, asset and benefactor registers, and foundation council minutes available in Panama; a virtual office provider may be retained solely for mail forwarding, with the statutory office remaining at the resident agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero: estimated residual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection at 5 percent to 10 percent annually for a low-risk PIF with no local payroll, no leased fixed assets and no regulated financial activity. Inspection triggers escalate if the foundation activates a Panama banking account, acquires a Panamanian merchant facility, or accumulates book assets exceeding US$1,000,000, where records must be producible within the SUSEF-mandated timeframe.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended; Articles 1, 5–8, 11–19, 23–25 and 53 govern creation, endowment, council, registered office, and tax treatment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones / Legal Entities Department (Public Registry of Panama)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva (Public Deed of Constitution) and certified inscription of the foundation in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama Private Interest Foundation has no statutory minimum paid-up capital. Law 25/1995 requires the founder to assign an initial endowment (patrimonio inicial) sufficient to carry out the foundation's purposes; a nominal US$500.00 is recorded as fully subscribed and contributed in the charter. No escrow account is legally mandated unless the foundation will administer regulated assets or trust funds; during formation the endowment is commonly held in a Panamanian attorney trust account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous Resolution of the Foundation Council. The Council, acting under Law 25 of 1995, resolves: (1) To acknowledge receipt of the founder's initial endowment of US$500.00, fully subscribed and paid. (2) To adopt the registered office at Calle 50, Obarrio, Suite 702, Panama, Republic of Panama, as the legal seat for statutory notices. (3) To appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each for five years, with authority to open bank and payment accounts and to execute service contracts. (4) To approve the formation registration and all municipal licensing steps relating to the customer-support helpdesk business. This resolution is immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry) – Name Reservation Bureau, Ancón, Panama City; also via online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for a 'Fundación de Interés Privado' with one to five proposed names. Pay the official reservation fee by bank receipt or online payment. The reservation certificate is valid for 60 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Application Form
Copy of founder's passport or identity card
Proof of payment of name reservation fee (approx. USD 60)
Notarized power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is rejected for confusing similarity, the agent may immediately refile using the alternate names, with no additional substantive fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Foundation Charter and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría Pública) engaged by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Panamanian counsel prepares the foundation charter (acta constitutiva) and bylaws in Spanish. The founder and first council members appear before the notary, who verifies identity, explains the deed, and acknowledges signatures, thereby creating the Escritura Pública.
required_dossiers: Draft of foundation charter and bylaws
Passports or identity cards of founder and initial council members
Name reservation certificate from Step 1
Legal fee and notarial invoice confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a legal or redrafting concern, the charter is amended and a new execution date is set before the same notary; this does not trigger a registry query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary presents the original Escritura Pública, an authenticated copy, and proof of payment of stamp taxes and registration fees for the formal inscription (matrícula). The registry assigns the foundation's registration number and returns a certified copy of the recorded deed.
required_dossiers: Original Escritura Pública con notarial acknowledgement
Authenticated copy of the deed for registry filing
Proof of payment of registry and stamp fees (approx. USD 350)
Granted name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a written objection, the attorney has 30 days to file a nota de enmienda (amendment note); if unresolved, a corrected deed is resubmitted with the reduced re-registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registration Certificate and Tax Identification Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, obtain a certified copy of the registered deed. File the RUC application with the DGI at the Ministry of Economy and Finance, supplying the foundational deed, council members' details, and office proof. The RUC certificate is delivered electronically and is required for invoicing and bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered foundation deed
Detailed list of council officers with addresses
Evidence of the registered office (lease or utility bill)
RUC application form and taxpayer declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI delays or disputes the registered office, the agent may provide an updated lease or domiciliation letter and resubmit; escalation to the DGI's customer service unit is available after 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice and Business Banking Launch
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal; Panama Digital (e-payment portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'Aviso de Operación' (Municipal Business Operation Notice) for the low-risk customer support and helpdesk activity, together with the RUC and certified foundation documents. Pay the municipal fee and obtain the municipal operating receipt; then the foundation may open commercial accounts and activate Stripe Billing and PayPal merchant rails.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation registration
RUC certificate issued by DGI
Lease agreement or domiciliation agent certificate
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Payment receipt for the municipal fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality treats the office as a full 'patente municipal,' the foundation may request reclassification by showing that the activity is a non-face-to-face SaaS helpdesk; alternatively, pay the 2% annual commercial rate and obtain the required compliance certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None for ISIC 6201; vertical industrial licensing is not applicable. The ordinary municipal regime administered by the Municipio de Panamá and the DGI covers service-based office operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Actividad Comercial o de Servicio (Municipal Business Operation Notice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAmbiente) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – based on Panamanian EIA classification, office-based IT and SaaS helpdesk activities do not require an environmental impact study, environmental registration, or environmental license where no industrial process is undertaken
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater and zero VOC emissions are generated by this activity. If the office produces only domestic sewage, it must meet the General Wastewater Discharge Standard (Executive Decree MD-389 of 2016) applicable to low-flow sanitary uses. No further atmospheric emission thresholds apply in the absence of manufacturing or fuel-combustion equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification are required through the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Panama Fire Department) before physical occupation. The office space must also pass the Municipality's structural load inspection and behavior-of-use review. Labor workplace clearance is obtained by filing the 'Registro de Salud y Seguridad Ocupacional' with MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral), confirming adequate emergency exits, lighting, ventilation, and ergonomic workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - General Directorate of Revenues, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); principal portal: official DGI website and Sede Electrónica e-tax single window. Ancillary authorities: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) for customs export declarations; Registro Público de Panamá for Private Interest Foundation (PIF) charter registration, corporate records and annual registry annuities; Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico (AIG) for issuance of the advanced electronic signature (Firma Electrónica Avanzada) required for e-tax filings. The tax system is unitary at the national level; Panama has no state or municipal income tax displacing DGI jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF, Ley 25 de 1995) is constituted by a foundation charter (Carta Fundacional) executed before a Panamanian notary and filed with the Registro Público, with a resident agent (Agente Residente), minimum initial endowment of B/.10,000 (USD 10,000, USD legal tender in Panama), one-time formation fee and annual registry annuity due by 30 June. DGI registration is triggered only when the foundation performs Panamanian-source taxable activity (Ley 25, Art. 4 restricts local commercial activity). When required, the PIF must: (i) obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI Sede Electrónica by submitting the registration application, certified foundation charter, identification of the founder and president, resident agent evidence and a Panamanian fiscal domicile; (ii) obtain the AIG advanced electronic signature before filing; (iii) register for ITBMS within 30 days of commencing taxable activities; and (iv) if exporting services, apply for DGI export-services status to claim zero-rating and input VAT refunds. A PIF receiving purely foreign-source helpdesk or SaaS subscription fees from non-domiciled clients, with the services performed and economically consumed abroad, is not required to obtain a RUC or file Panamanian ISR because Panama taxes only Panamanian-source income (Código Fiscal Art. 694).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: the PIF is an entity-level statutory vehicle that is neither transparent nor subject to entity-level income tax on foreign-source income; Panamanian-source income alone (services physically performed or economically exploited in Panama) falls within the 25% corporate ISR framework if the PIF conducts local commercial activities. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are not taxable on distributions of foreign-source foundation assets, and the PIF preserves the territorial exemption only while avoiding commercial activity inside Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box or US-style entity classification election; classification follows statutory form. Available elections include: (i) an election in the foundation charter to pursue Panamanian commercial activity and thereby become an ISR/ITBMS taxpayer or, alternatively, to remain a purely patrimonial offshore vehicle; (ii) voluntary ITBMS registration and election for DGI export-services status, permitting zero-rating of eligible helpdesk exports and reclaim of input ITBMS credits; (iii) the simplified small-taxpayer regime under Ley 66 de 2012 for low-turnover businesses (approximately B/.36,000 annual gross receipts), which simplifies ITBMS compliance but is not advantageous for exporters claiming credits; (iv) elective treatment of service fees as foreign-source under the DGI export-services framework where the contractual beneficiary and economic use are outside Panama. No hybrid-mismatch or comprehensive double-tax-treaty elections are available for this structure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, SBP). Panama has no issuing central bank; the SBP is the competent regulator for banking, foreign-exchange, and payment-system matters, with Banco Nacional de Panamá acting as fiscal agent and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas coordinating monetary policy under the full US-dollar legal-tender regime (Decreto Ley 9 de 1998 and Ley 21 de 2017).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the United States Dollar (USD) is the only circulating paper currency and the Balboa (PAB) exists solely as 1:1 subsidiary coinage. There are no exchange controls, no separate central-bank FX market, and no convertibility restrictions on either current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittances, dividend payments, interest, royalties, and PIF endowment distributions to founders or beneficiaries are unrestricted and are not subject to any exit, conversion, or withholding hurdle when the income is not of Panamanian source under the territorial tax regime. The only practical friction is bank-level AML/CFT documentation for large or high-velocity remittances, not governmental FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Because USD is national legal tender, Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. SaaS, helpdesk, and customer-support subscription proceeds may be retained offshore or held in any domestic USD account without central-bank repatriation, surrender, or conversion obligations. The only applicable discipline is standard SBP-regulated AML/CFT transaction monitoring by the collecting bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Panama's Law 163 of 2021 and SBP implementing rules permit locally licensed payment service companies (empresas de servicios de pago) to issue electronic money and access domestic clearing, but an offshore digital EMI (EEA/UK-licensed) is legally feasible only as a merchant collection node for Stripe Billing and PayPal Business flows; it cannot access Panama's local ACH or RTGS. The PIF should hold primary treasury liquidity in a Tier-1 Panamanian bank and sweep EMI settlement balances daily to reduce concentration risk. Material constraints: offshore EMIs are unlicensed in Panama, balances held with them are outside the Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos, and such balances must be classified as operational float rather than treasury assets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Private Interest Foundation, Tier-1 Panamanian banks generally require an in-person KYC interview at account opening in Panama City for the founder and at least one authorized foundation council member. Under SBP Acuerdo 3 de 2022 (single AML/CFT rule), fully remote digital onboarding is permissible for low-risk customers, so some banks accept video-conference completion of the signatory interview provided the original charter, council resolution, and passports are legalized via a licensed Panamanian registered agent and independently verified by e-KYC. Full remote opening without any physical touchpoint remains the exception and is reserved for simple structures whose founders reside in FATF-compliant high-transparency jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF structure perceived as opaque under Law 25 de 1995 (nominee council or beneficiaries not fully disclosed in public registry).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and Spanish-legalized foundation charter; sworn declaration of beneficiaries and founder; registered-agent certificate from a licensed Panamanian agent; legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming structure legality; AML/CFT declarations signed by each council member and signatory; certificate of good standing from the Public Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated settlement flows from Stripe and PayPal lacking a conventional invoice trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Stripe Billing and PayPal; platform settlement statements mapped to underlying client contracts; redacted customer invoices; written transaction-flow narrative; commitment to SBP Acuerdo 3 de 2022 record-retention obligations (five years) for all electronic-transfer documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder with no Panamanian tax residency and future cross-border endowment distributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Territorial-source income analysis demonstrating that helpdesk and SaaS services are performed and consumed outside Panama; DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) tax-registration attestation; audited or CPA-reviewed financial statements; founder's tax-residence certificate; documented source of the initial endowment; undertaking to support subsequent capital calls with clean-source evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity or client counterparties located in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OFAC/UN/EU sanctions-screening output; UBO and PEP declarations from all signatories; geographic-risk policy excluding restricted jurisdictions; contractual client representations; enhanced transaction-monitoring reports; sworn compliance statement from the resident agent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capitalization must be initiated by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for large value) from the founder's or investor's own bank account; third-party wires are rejected under standard PIF banking policy. The beneficiary name must exactly match the registered PIF name, and the remittance reference should state 'Apport capital - incremento de patrimonio fundacional' (capital contribution to foundation endowment). No exchange-control permit or central-bank approval is required; the receiving bank performs OFAC/AML screening and reconciles the remitter against the foundation charter and the SBP beneficial-ownership file before crediting. Documentary bundle: apostilled charter, registered-agent certificate, council resolution designating the account, source-of-funds declaration, and up-to-date KYC for each signatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the helpdesk SaaS (cloud hosting, data-center capacity, subcontracted support, software licenses) settle via: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct credits for international counterparties; (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 for procurement commitments above USD 50,000 or where vendors demand security; (iii) domestic USD ACH clearing through Panama's Cámara de Compensación Electrónica for onshore payments; and (iv) Stripe/PayPal payout rails for micro-disbursements. Domestic USD clearing is final on SBP-supervised rails, while international USD settlement completes over the US Fedwire/CHIPS network through the bank's US correspondent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot and forward contracts with onshore bank treasury desks (Banco General, Banistmo, Multibank) to convert EUR, GBP, and CAD receivables into USD at fixed future dates.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging Latin American currencies (COP, CLP, MXN, PEN, BRL) where the local deliverable market is thin, with USD cash settlement booked through the bank's international treasury desk.
Cross-currency swaps and FX options arranged through global desks (e.g., Citi Panama, Scotiabank Panama) to match multi-currency SaaS subscription receivables against a USD-dominated cost base.
Natural/operational hedging via a multi-currency settlement account and periodic conversion sweeps, reducing the notional of standalone derivative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundation (Tasa Única)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 1% per month, a 10% surcharge, denial of good standing certificates, and administrative strike-off from the Public Registry if unpaid for more than two consecutive years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not statutorily required for a Private Interest Foundation unless (i) the foundation's charter mandates independent audit, or (ii) the foundation carries on commercial activities in Panama with gross taxable income exceeding USD 2.25 million (under Law 108/2008).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama GAAP; IFRS for entities whose charter or local law requires audited financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2021, the Resident Agent must collect and confirm the ultimate beneficial ownership data of the Foundation on an annual basis (by 31 January each year). Updates must be filed within 15 days of any change; non-compliance attracts monetary penalties and suspension of the Foundation's good standing status.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Resolutions of the Foundation Council and General Assembly)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on Panama-source net taxable income (Código Fiscal Art. 699; Ley 8 de 2010); 0% on foreign-source income under Panama's territorial tax system.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundation (Ley 25 de 1995, as amended) exemption: distributions, capital transfers, and all acts performed or effects arising outside Panama are tax-exempt at 0%; accordingly, foreign-sourced helpdesk/SaaS revenue collected via Stripe/PayPal and settled outside Panama is effectively exempt. Panama-source business income remains taxable at 25% with deductions for ordinary and necessary expenses; qualifying ICT R&D and export-service investments may access specific deduction and reinvestment benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (Declaración Anual de Renta) — filed electronically via the SIT (Sistema de Información Tributaria) at sit.dgi.gob.pa using the RUC and electronic credentials. Ancillary annual filing: Informe/Declaración de Beneficiario Final submitted through the Registro Público portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ends 31 December unless a different date is lawfully fixed in the Foundation Charter; Form 101 is due within four months of fiscal year-end according to the RUC last-digit schedule (endings 1–5: March; endings 6–0: April–15 June). Non-resident PIFs with no Panama-source activity may file a zero return on the same schedule; there is no extension for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 103 / Línea 1a — Ingresos brutos (gross Panamanian-source revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross receipts from business activity physically or economically carried out in Panama, before deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 where 100% of helpdesk subscriptions are billed, processed, and settled offshore (Stripe, PayPal) with no contracts, staff, servers, or offices in Panama

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source revenue exempt under the territorial system and under Ley 25 de 1995
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the foreign-source turnover and attach an explanatory note evidencing offshore origin: foreign IP logs, foreign settlement currency statements, absence of a Panama permanent establishment, and board minutes confirming offshore management

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and allocable expenses attributable to Panama-source revenue (hosting, licensed conversational AI APIs, foreign staff, amortisation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave nil for the zero return; if a Panama branch operates, deduct only expenses supported by invoices (facturas) and never allocate group overhead in excess of an arm's-length charge

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 119 / Línea 3 — Renta neta gravable (net taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income minus permitted deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 0.00 for the zero return; effective CIT exposure on foreign cloud-helpdesk fees is nil unless the DGI recharacterises the activity as Panama-source

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying 25% to net taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 0.00 for the zero filing; advance tax payments (anticipos) may be credited against the gross tax where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 14 — Nota Ley 25 de 1995 (Distribuciones de la Fundación)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distributions of foundation assets to beneficiaries are outside the definition of dividend and are not taxable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not report beneficiary distributions as dividend income; such distributions are gratuitous transfers of foundation assets and remain exempt under the PIF statute

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: automatic fine under Art. 712 Código Fiscal of 5% of the tax due (minimum B/.50, maximum B/.5,000), plus a monthly surcharge (recargo) of 10% of the unpaid tax per month (capped at 100% of the original tax); fraudulent zero filing of Panama-source revenue triggers criminal evasion sanctions and the statutory default interest at the legal rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Corporate distributions: 5% withholding where profits have borne Panama CIT; 10% where profits were exempt or untaxed (Art. 733 Código Fiscal). Private Interest Foundation distributions are not dividends and are exempt from both the 5%/10% dividend tax and from remittance withholding to non-resident beneficiaries.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network (incl. Mexico, Netherlands, Spain, UAE, UK, Luxembourg, Singapore, Portugal, France, Italy, South Korea, Qatar) applies only where: (i) the non-resident holds a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, translated/legalised where required; (ii) the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration are delivered to the Panamanian payer or the DGI before or at the date of payment; (iii) the payer then applies the reduced treaty rate (commonly 5%–10% on interest/royalties and 5% on dividends under certain DTAs) and retains the TRC in the withholding file for five years; absent a TRC, the statutory rate must be withheld, with refund obtainable only by administrative claim within the limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties/technical-service fees: statutory 12.5% withholding (Art. 750 et seq. Código Fiscal) where the IP is used or the service exploited in Panama and payment leaves the country; DTAs commonly cap royalties at 10% (e.g., Spain, UK) and interest at 5% (e.g., Netherlands, Spain). Non-treaty interest paid to non-resident lenders carries no Panamanian WHT, but interest on related-party debt above the 3:1 debt-to-equity thin-cap ratio is recharacterised as a deemed dividend and taxed at 5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 73 of 2021: mandatory annual TP Declaration and Local File are triggered where the taxpayer's Panama-source gross income exceeds PAB 3,000,000 in the prior fiscal year, or where controlled transactions with related parties located in low-/no-tax jurisdictions exceed PAB 1,000,000; Master File documentation applies to members of MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least PAB 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 235 of 2022 (Panama ESR) apply to PIFs carrying on a relevant activity — including technology and helpdesk services — performed in Panama. A PIF must evidence, via an annual Substantial Presence Statement, the presence and proportionality of a local registered office, resident employees, physical assets, and board/management autonomy, and must file the declaration within the statutory calendar. A pure offshore helpdesk arrangement with no employees, office, or management in Panama remains outside ESR only if contracts are demonstrably concluded and executed outside Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Bookkeeping helpdesk revenue in a Panama-registered PIF while servicing Panamanian customers through local subcontractors or a Panamanian office, routing settlement funds through foreign Stripe/PayPal accounts, and filing a zero Form 101 on the foreign-source claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full Panama-source income; 10% monthly surcharge plus late-payment interest; criminal tax evasion under the Código Penal: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for the responsible legal representative, plus a fine equal to 100%–300% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable; the civil fraud exception to patrimonial separation lifts the PIF veil, exposing the founder's and beneficiaries' personal assets, and the DGI's coercive collection regime may issue travel bans against directors for unpaid assessed tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee-only PIF with no physical presence, no employees, and a mailbox address to invoice multi-million-dollar helpdesk AI services while all management decisions are dictated from the foreign founder's jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Annulled tax exemptions and recharacterisation of the PIF as a taxable Panama permanent establishment; ESR monetary penalty of PAB 10,000–100,000; strike-off of the foundation from the Registro Público; possible freezing of foundation bank accounts upon adverse FATF/AML findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts disregard legal personality where the foundation is a sham or mask used for abuse of law; directors and the registered agent risk administrative penalties under Law 23 of 2015 and disqualification, with possible personal criminal exposure for aiding misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and continuously verify the founder, council members, and beneficiaries behind the PIF's payment rails; channelling helpdesk licence fees to opaque foreign shell recipients; failing to file the annual beneficial-owner declaration with the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 de 2015 sanctions: fines up to PAB 1,000,000 per unverified operation; deregistration of the registered agent; money-laundering predicate offence under Criminal Code Art. 254 punishable by imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for the beneficial owner and executive officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability applies to council members who knowingly conceal the economic beneficiary; the corporate veil is inapplicable in money-laundering cases, and travel bans (impedimento de salida) are routinely imposed during parallel DGI/AML proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing excessive non-arm's-length group fees to the Panama helpdesk entity for software/API and AI-bot licences, or funding the PIF with unaudited shareholder loans exceeding the 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio, thereby eliminating Panama taxable income while failing to retain CUP/TNMM documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment to the arm's-length price; denial of interest deductions on the excess portion; recharacterisation as a deemed dividend subject to 5% WHT; penalty of 10% of the adjusted tax plus interest at the legal rate; additional fine of up to PAB 50,000 for non-submission of the TP declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for deliberate under-pricing where they authorised the related-party contracts and signed the tax declaration; the DGI may disregard the foundation separation defence under the fraud exception and execute directly on the directors' personal assets.
